title: fix(metadata-protocol): a packaged flow's refusal names the clone and the on/off switch, not a redeploy or OS_METADATA_WRITABLE (#20819)
body:
Fixes #20819
Clause-②: no

## What changes

When a write or a removal targets a flow that a code package ships, without naming that package with `?package=`, the package doors in `packages/metadata-protocol` refuse it with `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`. (A write that names the shipping package takes the named-base limb and is refused `403 ITEM_LOCKED`, unchanged by this PR; corrected by the seat after review 5916639859.) The refusal's sentence is now chosen **per ADR-0126 regime**, from one table keyed on the type's declared regime:

- `PACKAGED_BASE_REGIME` (`protocol.ts:14704`) is the regime declaration. It holds `flow: 'C'` and nothing else.
- `PACKAGED_BASE_REFUSAL_BY_REGIME` (`protocol.ts:14732`) is the per-regime sentence table. It has one row, Regime C.
- `packagedBaseRegimeSentence` (`protocol.ts:14749`) looks up the table. The two emitters, `refusePackagedBaseOverride` for save and `refusePackagedBaseRemoval` for delete, ask it for their sentence and fall back to their old literal, which is kept byte for byte. There is no `type === 'flow'` branch in the emitters.

The Regime C sentence, as served by `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/pkg_alert_flow`:

```text
Metadata item 'flow/pkg_alert_flow' is provided by a code package, and its packaged base is locked against in-place edits. Clone it under a new name to customize it (POST /api/v1/automation/:name/clone, body {name, label}), or switch it off (POST /api/v1/automation/:name/toggle, body {enabled: false}; operator-only where one install serves several organizations). See docs/adr/0126-packaged-metadata-customization-model.md.
```

On removal, "against in-place edits" reads "against removal". The sentence names the clone (§7.1) and the switch (§7.2), cites ADR-0126, and does not mention `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` or a redeploy.

**What does not move** (Clause-② `no`): the code, the status, and which writes are refused. The predicate is unchanged, and `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=flow` still opens the lock at both doors (the existing hatch pin stays green; only its comment changed). The named-base `ITEM_LOCKED` limb is unchanged. Every type with no declared regime keeps its sentence byte for byte.

## Zone 2 readings (PM hypotheses)

- **H1 held.** `packagedBaseRefusal` is at `protocol.ts:14513` (about `:14506` at base `33b6e8bec`). Every door reaches the same two emitters, and every caller relays the sentence unchanged:
  - `saveMetaItem` / `deleteMetaItem` call the emitters directly, behind `environmentId !== undefined`.
  - `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` returns `packagedBaseRefusal` for a flow in the loader's set. It is asked by `saveMetaItem` (the `/meta` PUT, on both topologies) and by runtime `refuseUnauthoredFlowWrite` (`POST /automation`, `PUT /automation/:name`, and the clone target). The runtime relays it through `deps.errorFromThrown(refusal)`.
  - runtime `refusePackagedFlowBaseChange` covers `DELETE /automation/:name`, and PUT/POST when the protocol has no authoring rule. It relays through `deps.errorFromThrown(refusal)`.
  - The REST `/meta` routes relay it through `handleRouteError`, verbatim below 500 characters.
  - The runtime pin "ONE emitter" compares the messages across the doors, and they are equal.
- **H2: no regime is declared in code.** `git grep -i regime` over `packages/{spec,metadata-protocol,metadata-core,runtime,core,types}/src` finds prose comments only. `DEFAULT_METADATA_TYPE_REGISTRY` entries carry no regime field. So the smallest declaration went in beside the door: a map from type to regime, holding Regime C = `flow`.
  - ADR-0126 §3's full Regime C list: `flow`; `permission`; `action` (the disable half; the clone half is not chartered, §8 item 2); pre-charted `tool`, `skill` and `position`.
  - Two other Regime C types reach this door. `action` reaches it on save and delete. `permission` reaches it on save only: its delete is exempted by the `supportsOverlay` carve-out.
  - Neither is declared. The Regime C sentence names the `/automation` routes, which exist for a flow alone. `action`'s switch is `POST /api/v1/actions/_activation/:object/:action` and it has no clone; `permission` has its own clone machinery.
  - `tool`, `skill` and `position` reach the door only if a package ships one. The measurement recorded in `isNestedArtifactField`'s comment found none on the showcase.
  - The `action` control pin holds the undeclared sentence byte-identical. Measured at the REST route, see the Acceptance notes.
- **H3 held.** Both routes are served on `main`: `POST /automation/:name/toggle` at `automation.ts:2427` and `POST /automation/:name/clone` at `automation.ts:2513`, under the `/automation` domain prefix.
  - The toggle is gated by `manage_metadata`, then by `refuseUngrantedActivationWrite`, which requires the platform operator in the `group` / `isolated` postures (ADR-0126 §5).
  - The clone body `{ name, label }` needs both keys. The toggle body is `{ enabled?: boolean }`.
  - The runtime test's "what the lock leaves open" cases drive both routes to `200` on a packaged flow.
- **H4 applies, and it holds.** `CLIENT_MESSAGE_MAX = 500` (`packages/rest/src/error-response.ts:72`) truncates the tail at 500 characters.
  - The sentence is 411 characters before the name on save and 404 on removal: 425 and 418 with `pkg_alert_flow`. Any name up to 88 characters arrives whole.
  - The protocol pin asserts a length under 500. The REST pin asserts the served text still ends with the ADR citation.

## Tests (all at head `d58d5578f6` unless stated)

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.packaged-base-refusal.test.ts`, with 8 new cases:
  - flow save and delete, on both topologies: 403 `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, clone and toggle named, ADR-0126 cited, no hatch, no redeploy, under 500 characters;
  - the plural spelling folds to the same sentence;
  - the `/meta` doors throw the regime sentence;
  - control: `page` keeps its sentence byte for byte;
  - control: `action` keeps its save and delete sentences byte for byte.
  Result: `Tests 17 passed (17)`.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-packaged-base-lock.test.ts`: `PUT` and `DELETE /automation/:name` (both topologies) and `POST /automation` onto a packaged name now also assert that the relayed message names clone and toggle and does not name the hatch. The hatch test's title and comment are corrected: the refusal no longer names the hatch, and the hatch still opens the door. `Tests 15 passed (15)`.
- `packages/rest/src/rest-meta-packaged-flow-refusal.test.ts` (new) drives the real `PUT` / `DELETE /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` routes over a real protocol and `SchemaRegistry`: flow PUT on both topologies, flow DELETE on an environment kernel, and a `page` control compared byte for byte. `Tests 4 passed (4)`.
- Full `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` suite, run at `af8a9ee7a9` (the merge since then brought no change to this package): `Test Files 193 passed | 3 skipped (196)`, `Tests 2870 passed | 19 skipped (2889)`.
- Typecheck at `af8a9ee7a9`: `pnpm --filter` `typecheck` passes for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/runtime`. `tsc --listFiles` counts each of the three test files once in its package's program. `check:test-typecheck` is OK for rest (0 held) and runtime (the identity-pinned ledger is unchanged).
- The `packages/cli` tiers were not touched. The runtime and rest full suites are left to CI; this PR changes only the one test file in each.

## Ablation on the regime choice (committed fix first; `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with its restore trap, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol build`, then `node scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`; rest and runtime read the `dist/`)

Predicted before running: leg A turns the flow pins red and leaves the controls green; leg B turns only the `page` controls red. Both came out as predicted.

| leg | on-disk proof | dist preflight | metadata-protocol | runtime | rest |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A: delete `flow: 'C',` | anchor 1→0, blob `f1e6267e`→`787e1532` | marker absent from all 24 built files | 5 failed / 12 passed | 5 failed / 10 passed | 3 failed / 1 passed |
| A restore | blob == HEAD `f1e6267e`, `git diff HEAD` empty | marker present in 2 built files; tree clean | 17 passed | 15 passed | 4 passed |
| B: declare `page: 'C'` | anchor 1→0, blob `f1e6267e`→`fbb29b3b` | marker present in 2 built files | 1 failed (`page` control) / 16 passed | 15 passed | 1 failed (`page` control) / 3 passed |
| B restore | blob == HEAD, `git status --porcelain` empty | marker absent from all 24; tree clean | 17 passed | 15 passed | 4 passed |

The first leg-B attempt was a no-op: `ablation-replace` refused it because the replacement contained the anchor ("anchor count moved 1 → 1") and restored the file. It was re-run with a non-overlapping anchor, and the row above is that run. Both runs were at `af8a9ee7a9`.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths), at `d58d5578f6`, derived 63 commands. The change set is 5 paths, 366 changed lines against the 5000-line human-merge threshold: under. All 63 were run at `d58d5578f6`, and `--ran` reports: `✓ dispatch-gates --ran: 63 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 61 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (0 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3, 2 claimed)`.

- 61 exited 0, including `check:doc-authoring` (the new sentence carries no tracker number), `check:nul-bytes`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:cross-package-test-inputs`, `check:test-source-alias`, `check:issue-citations` and `check:durability-log-level`.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt`, reason: PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3). Both read the whole workspace's built output. A full packages build is 50 uncached turbo tasks, `@objectstack/console` included (dry run), which is beyond the shared box's foreground cap. CI's lint.yml builds that closure first.
- The branch merged `origin/main` (`d58d5578f6`) because the first derivation warned of a stale tree (`scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` had moved). The incoming commits touch `driver-memory` and that script only. The re-derivation printed the same 63 commands with no stale warning. The build closure was refreshed and the three pinned files re-run at `d58d5578f6` (17 / 15 / 4 passed).

Lint was narrowed to the changed files, not the repo-wide `pnpm lint` (that run is CI's). Three pieces of evidence make that narrowing complete:
1. The population comes from eslint's own config: `eslint --no-inline-config --print-config` resolves a config for each of the 4 changed `.ts` files, so none is ignored.
2. `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on those files counts `files 4 errors 0 warnings 0`, at `d58d5578f6`.
3. `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting ("no `parserOptions.project`, no typed `@typescript-eslint` rules", at its line 328), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it did not touch.

## Acceptance notes

- **Other Regime C types keep the hatch sentence (measured; not filed here).** ADR-0126 §3 also puts `action` and `permission` in Regime C. Driving the real REST `/meta` route in-process (real protocol, registry double, environment kernel) gives these answers:
  - `PUT /api/v1/meta/action/pkg_approve` answers `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` with "Edit the source artifact and redeploy, or set OS_METADATA_WRITABLE to grant a runtime escape hatch. See docs/adr/0005-…";
  - `PUT /api/v1/meta/permission/pkg_perm` gives the same answer;
  - `DELETE` on the action answers the removal sentence, which names no path at all.
  The ruling scoped this card to `flow`. Their own sanctioned paths differ (see H2), so they need their own table rows. That is left to the seat, together with #15206, which owns whether the hatch survives for sealed managed content.
- **The named-base `ITEM_LOCKED` limb** (`SysMetadataRepository.readOnlyBaseOverrideError`, `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1745`, shared with the repository door) still prescribes "Edit the source artifact and redeploy, or set OS_METADATA_WRITABLE=TYPE" for any type, flow included, and cites ADR-0010. It is reached by `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/:name?package=PKG` when PKG is read-only. Reach NOT MEASURED: the harness's engine double reports every package as writable, so the probe got this PR's `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` sentence instead. It is outside this card's file surface. Carrier: none.
- `orgScopedWriteRefusal` and the code-only refusals also name the hatch. They answer different conditions (an org-scoped write of any flow; code-only types), and whether the hatch survives is #15206's question.

## Deviations

- Commit trailers use the model-free pair from AGENTS.md, not the model-bearing trailer the harness suggested.
- One merge commit (`d58d5578f6`) from `origin/main`; see Gates.
